_name: probe-2026-09-25-reviewer-live - the graph reviewer fires live on the shapes it was built for, and stays quiet on the rest
_why:
On the 2026-09-25 dev run the graph reviewer ran on 25 of 25 graph turns and fired on none: the live catalog read two uncached value lists per turn, so unapplied_value never reached T_A_ALN.DataType (fix/reviewer-live-values). This probe asserts the reviewer's own output on the debug payload: debug.graph_review.verdict, debug.graph_review.fired (a list of check names, added by that branch; absent before it, so every should-fire criterion is red on an older build, which is the point) and debug.suggestions (the chips; absent when there are none, so `eq null` means no chip). Five should-fire shapes on dev data (unapplied_value twice, one with the chip clicked as turn 2, negated_value and value_split as plain counts, premise_count) and four quiet controls (a grouped spellings count, a plain count, an applied equality, and the 'Only RNA-Seq' chip's own text, which must resolve to 10,517 and stay quiet). Every should-fire case depends on the graph agent writing the shape the reviewer checks: if it applies the filter itself (DataType = 'RNA-Seq', Ethnicity = 'hispanic or latino'), the reviewer is right to stay quiet and the case reads as drift, not a reviewer defect. For agent C: rev.unapplied_rnaseq_alignment repeats corpus case tcga.patients_with_rnaseq and rev.quiet_unc_spellings repeats tcga.unc_center_spellings; fold these criteria into those cases rather than asking twice, and pick one of the two unapplied_value cases if the seed must not near-repeat. rev.quiet_chip_text_resolves is the chip's click text; keep it only if a near-repeat of the RNA-Seq case is acceptable.
  manage.py nessie --tier full --cases /app/NessieAI/tests/nessie_tests/probes/probe-2026-09-25-reviewer-live.json --out /app/runs/reviewer-live-<date>
PAID: 9 cases, 10 NS turns, no Container-CC. Needs the operator's approval for the run. Dev only: every case is TCGA data, which production does not hold.
_instance_warning:
EVERY NUMBER HERE WAS MEASURED ON fairdata-dev ON 2026-09-25 (read-only, admin; scoped to project 1 the TCGA numbers are the same). Re-pin before a run on another graph:
  python NessieAI/tests/nessie_tests/scripts/pin_probe_truths.py --emit-cypher <this file>
  python ... pin_probe_truths.py --pin <this file> --from measured.json
_observability: graph_review.fired, graph_review.verdict and suggestions are read from query_complete.debug by dotted path (NessieAI/tests/e2e/criteria.py resolve_field: dicts only, so the fired list, not the checks list). A `matches_re` on suggestions reads the chips' Python repr: 'Only RNA-Seq' and 'expected_count': 10517. graph_review.lookups (what the live catalog read, what the budget stopped) is informational: no criterion reads it, the triage does.

reviewer_live.description: Single NS graph turns whose debug payload shows the graph reviewer firing (with its disclosure and chip) or staying quiet, on the dev graph's TCGA data.

variants.name: unapplied_value: RNA-Seq alignments counted with miRNA-Seq, the mix named, and a click on 'Only RNA-Seq' reruns the reviewer's statement
variants._why: The dev 1276 shape. Operator ruling 2026-09-25: 10,761 is an acceptable answer, but the reply must say it mixes RNA-Seq and miRNA-Seq and offer 'Only RNA-Seq' (expected 10,517). Dev: patients split by alignment DataType miRNA-Seq 10,561, RNA-Seq 10,517, WXS 3. Turn 2 clicks the chip: the harness sends the chip's exact text on the very next turn, which is how the chat panel sends a click, so the server reruns the reviewer's own statement (debug.chip_rerun.mode 'direct') with no entity agent, parser or graph agent, and offers no chip back. If turn 1 offered no chip (the graph agent applied DataType itself), turn 2 is an ordinary question and its click criteria are red, correctly.

turns.label: main
turns.query: How many TCGA patients have at least one RNA-Seq alignment derived from their samples?

turns.label: click
turns.query: How many TCGA patients have at least one RNA-Seq alignment derived from their samples? Count only Sequence Alignment Analysis records whose DataType is RNA-Seq.

variants.name: unapplied_value: a WGS alignment question the query answers for every alignment type
variants._why: The same omission on another value. Dev: TCGA patients with any alignment derived from their samples 11,171, with a WGS one 9,447 (by DataType: WXS 10,610, miRNA-Seq 10,561, RNA-Seq 10,517, WGS 9,447, ATAC-Seq 404). The chip's expected count depends on the Cypher shape (set when the alignment is bound only inside an EXISTS), so only the chip label is asserted.

turns.label: main
turns.query: How many TCGA patients have at least one WGS alignment derived from their samples?

variants.name: negated_value: a count of 'Hispanic' also counts 'not hispanic or latino'
variants._why: Dev T_PAT.Ethnicity: 'not hispanic or latino' 8,491, 'hispanic or latino' 401, so CONTAINS 'hispanic' counts 8,892. A count with no grouping column fires since 3422cb1c (before it, a count counted as already stating the split). The chip 'Only hispanic or latino' carries no expected count (no Tier 2 count for this check); a click on it goes to the graph agent with the turn's statement and the one change.

turns.label: main
turns.query: How many TCGA patients are Hispanic?

variants.name: value_split: a count of 'STAR' alignments counts three aligner modes
variants._why: Dev T_A_ALN.Aligner: STAR 2-Pass Genome 11,505, STAR 2-Pass Chimeric 10,861, STAR 2-Pass Transcriptome 10,861 (33,227 in all). A count with no grouping column fires value_split_catalog since 3422cb1c.

turns.label: main
turns.query: How many TCGA alignments were made with the STAR aligner?

variants.name: premise_count: the user states a set size the graph does not hold
variants._why: The dev graph holds 11,428 TCGA patients, 5,817 of them female. The question states 12,000: the reviewer discloses that the search did not reproduce that number, with no chip.

turns.label: main
turns.query: Of the 12,000 TCGA patients, how many are female?

variants.name: quiet: a grouped count already states every spelling
variants._why: The dev 1273 control: 'UNC' 28,242, 'unc.edu' 1,049, 'UNC-LCCC' 104 alignments. The rows are the split, so no value check may fire.

turns.query: Which spellings of the UNC (University of North Carolina) sequencing center are used on TCGA alignment samples, and how many alignments carry each spelling?

variants.name: quiet: a plain count of a study's patients
variants._why: The dev 1274 control: 617 patients in the TCGA glioblastoma study.

variants.name: quiet: the value the question names is applied
variants._why: 5,817 female TCGA patients on dev. 'female' is also a STOP_VALUES word, so unapplied_value never reads it; the control is that nothing else fires.

turns.label: main
turns.query: How many TCGA patients are female?

variants.name: quiet: the 'Only RNA-Seq' chip's own text gets the narrowed count and no chip of its own
variants._why: What one click on rev.unapplied_rnaseq_alignment's chip sends (NARROW_QUERY in graph_review.py). The filter is spelled out, so the graph agent applies DataType and the reviewer stays quiet: 10,517, and chips never chain.
